instructions: Assess each supplied resource for practical TSO usefulness using the supplied guidance. Use only these saved facts; do not browse, use tools, contact anyone or read other chats. Return JSON only with assignmentSha256, complete (boolean), and cases. Each case needs caseId, decision (retain/reserve/exclude/needs-check), reason, criticalDetails (array of strings), and openQuestions (array of strings). Account for every case. Preserve usable named referrals and consequential eligibility, cost and timing details. Do not invent provider facts or human approval.

resource.name: Phoenix Electrical JATC · Paid Electrician Apprenticeship
resource.description: Train as an electrician while working for a contractor. Admission is competitive, and both application and training fees apply.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
A four-year program combines paid work with classroom training. Selected apprentices are assigned to a participating contractor.

**Eligibility Requirements**
You must be 18 by the start and meet education and algebra requirements or approved alternatives. Identification and school records are needed. Some military service or documented electrical experience can qualify for exceptions. You must be able to reach regional work sites. Work can involve ladders, confined spaces and regular lifting of 50 pounds; ask the program about its essential job requirements and accommodations.

**How to Best Connect**
Use How to Apply on the program website. Email webservices@pejatc.org for application help or to arrange use of a training-center computer.

**Access**
Training centers are in Phoenix; work sites vary across the program area. Classes accompany full-time work. Check the current application deadline before paying.

**Important Information to Know**
Published charges are a $40 nonrefundable application fee and $187 monthly during training. Confirm current costs. Applying does not guarantee selection.
resource.address: Phoenix training centers; regional job sites

resource.name: SCSEP · Paid Job Training for Adults 55 and Older
resource.description: Part-time paid community-service training for unemployed older adults with low income. A local program office checks eligibility and available places.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Train with a nonprofit or public agency while gaining work experience and job-search help. Training is usually about 20 hours a week.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Arizona residents 55 or older who are unemployed, eligible to work, have income at or below 125% of the federal poverty level and face a job barrier. Examples include limited English, disability or poor job prospects. Staff check eligibility; Arizona Job Connection registration is required.

**How to Best Connect**
DES lists 602-841-0403 for its Maricopa AARP/Easterseals route. It also lists AARP at 928-395-2261 and NICOA at 505-292-2001 for Maricopa County. Call a grantee to confirm current Mesa intake and available places.

**Access**
Serves eligible Maricopa County residents, including Mesa. The office arranges host-agency training; confirm where you would need to travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Training usually averages 20 hours weekly, paid at the highest applicable minimum wage. It is temporary training, with limited places and possible waiting lists. Ask about participation limits and how the wages affect your benefits before enrolling.

resource.name: Express Employment Professionals · Mesa Staffing Office
resource.description: Helps you find temporary, part-time or full-time work with local employers. There is no job placement fee. Call for help applying by phone or in person.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
One application connects you with several employers. Jobs may include warehouse and manufacturing work, skilled trades, office and customer service work, and professional roles. Temporary, evaluation-hire and direct-hire options depend on current openings. Express offers weekly pay and free online job-search resources. ExpressLearn courses are for workers employed by Express. Some workers qualify for health-plan options, dental, vision, life and disability coverage, retirement benefits and confidential counseling.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requirements depend on the job, including experience, skills, schedule and any required license. Some jobs require a skills assessment. Placement depends on a suitable opening. Some benefits require a minimum number of hours or weeks worked; ask which benefits you qualify for, what they cover and what you would pay.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-820-3700 to arrange help with an application by phone or in person, or email jobs.mesaaz@expresspros.com. You can also apply online. Have your work and education history, references and contact details ready. Bring work-eligibility documents to an interview; ask which documents you need. If you create an online account, submit your application to the Mesa office; saving an account alone does not send it.

**Access**
849 N. Dobson Rd., Suite 107, Mesa, AZ 85201. Office hours: Monday–Thursday, 8 AM–5 PM; Friday, 8 AM–3 PM. Call before visiting to arrange application help. Job locations vary by employer.

**Important Information to Know**
Job placement is free. Before accepting work, ask about the pay, schedule, work location, transportation and any required equipment or testing costs. Openings change; applying does not guarantee a job. After an assignment ends, contact the office to be considered for another one.
resource.address: 849 N. Dobson Rd., Suite 107, Mesa, AZ 85201
resource.hours: Monday–Thursday 8 AM–5 PM; Friday 8 AM–3 PM

resource.name: Copa Health · Disability Employment Support
resource.description: Help for people with disabilities to prepare for work and find or keep a job. Start by asking about a referral and funding.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Career planning, work preparation, computer skills, job development and supported employment are offered. Services can include community work experience and ongoing support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services support people with disabilities. Entry and funding depend on the program and referral; VR, DDD, behavioral-health plans and private pay are listed.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Copa at 480-969-3800 and ask for Employment Related Services. If you have a case manager, DDD support coordinator or VR counselor, ask about a referral. Referrals go to referrals@copahealth.org. Confirm which service and funding approval you need.

**Access**
Copa lists employment services at two Mesa sites and other Valley locations. Its main office is at 924 N. Country Club Dr., Mesa; call for the correct employment site before traveling. Transportation to community group work sites is offered; ask separately about getting to your intake or training office.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm your service, funding, any cost and whether the work placement pays you. Copa’s web page describes what businesses pay Copa; that does not establish a participant’s wage. Facility training, group work experience and competitive job support differ.
resource.phone: 480-969-3800 (Copa main office; ask for Employment Related Services)

resource.name: St. Mary’s Food Bank · Culinary, Warehouse and Forklift Training
resource.description: Free nine-week training for food-service or warehouse work. Applicants must be able to attend full weekday classes and meet screening requirements.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Community Kitchen teaches culinary skills. LIFT teaches logistics, inventory and forklift skills. Both help prepare adults facing employment barriers for work.

**Eligibility Requirements**
You must be 18+, authorized to work, facing employment barriers and ready for steady work. Background and drug screening apply, including random drug tests; arson and registered-sex-offender exclusions are published. You must attend consistently and live in a shelter, your own or rented home, or a halfway house. Ask about eligibility if your living arrangement is different.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-343-3183 for application help. Apply online, drop off an application or fax it to 480-780-3799. Staff arrange an interview and tell you whether you are accepted, waitlisted or declined.

**Access**
Training is at 3003 W. Thomas Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85017. Classes meet Monday–Friday, 7 AM–3 PM, for nine weeks. Consider the daily trip from Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
Training is free. Housing is not included, and employment is not guaranteed. Ask staff to explain the screening and living-arrangement rules before applying.

resource.name: St. Vincent de Paul · Job Readiness and Workforce Housing
resource.description: Job preparation and temporary paid work connected with housing programs, plus workforce housing for people working toward stability. Ask which services can be reached from Mesa.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Resume and job-search help, work skills and case management. Neighborhood Brigade offers temporary paid cleanup work for residents of Ozanam Manor and Washington Street housing. Rosalie’s Place offers workforce housing with employment and money-management support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Paid crew jobs are tied to specified SVdP housing programs. Workforce housing serves adults working or looking for work; staff screen applicants. Ask separately whether job-search services are available without entering housing.

**How to Best Connect**
Housing screening: 602-850-6900, 8 AM-3 PM. A phone screening is followed by an in-person interview. Rosalie’s Place questions: 602-261-6870, Monday-Friday, 8 AM-3 PM. Mesa Dining Room: 602-619-9411; ask whether job help is offered there and when.

**Access**
Rosalie’s Place is at 320 W. Watkins Rd., Phoenix. Mesa Dining Room, 49 W. Broadway Rd., is listed among work-readiness locations; ask about the actual local service and schedule before going for job help. Washington Street shelter requires a partner referral and does not accept walk-ups.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the agreement before accepting housing. Rosalie’s workforce page describes free housing and saving 60% of net income; the general intake page says residents with income pay 30%. Ask which rules apply to your program. Beds and paid crew openings are limited.
resource.address: Rosalie’s Place and Ozanam Manor: 320 W. Watkins Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85003; Washington Street shelter: 2739 E. Washington St., Phoenix, AZ 85034. Call about intake before visiting.
